answer: The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. Because the vertex measurement is attested to the willow verifier, the river audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. A farm needs 11 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. Each copy needs 2 hours of work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
